clue.text: Arrived with character in Arthur's place

parts.note: arrived means came
a lot is a character, as in 'a bad lot'

explanation.surface: Someone turns up with an odd personality at King Arthur's home.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the court of King Arthur and his knights was held at this castle.

clue.text: Praise collapse

definitions.meaning: to crack someone up is to praise them highly
to break down under strain, or into laughter

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to talk something up and to suffer a breakdown.

clue.text: Maximise-your opportunity

parts.note: a description of getting full value from a chance, read as an everyday phrase

explanation.definitionFit: Exploiting a chance fully is to get the greatest benefit from it.

clue.text: Haul up the tool

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word tool is read from bottom to top

explanation.definitionFit: A haul of stolen goods is plunder or booty.

clue.text: Easiest way to deal with sheets after ironing twice as much

definitions.text: Easiest way to deal with sheets after ironing
definitions.meaning: sheets are folded in half to be put away
double the amount

explanation.definitionFit: Folding sheets in half is the easiest way, and doubled means twice as much.

clue.text: Breezy correspondence

parts.note: breezy suggests letters from a device that makes a breeze, a fan, rather than cheerful ones

explanation.walkthrough: 'Breezy' looks like a word for light-hearted letters; read it as letters coming from something that blows air, and you get the post admirers send to a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters sent by admirers to a star are a kind of correspondence, and a fan makes a breeze.

clue.text: Cargo for French rowing team

parts.note: French gives FR
an eight is a racing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A load meant for a crew of French rowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by ship, plane or train are this.

clue.text: Throat or cheek

definitions.meaning: the part of the body joining head and shoulders
impudence or nerve, as in 'what a nerve'

explanation.definitionFit: The body part around the throat, and brass nerve or impudence, share this word.

clue.text: High flier needs pneumatic pressure from refrigerator

parts.note: pneumatic means worked by air
pressure is force
off means from, as in 'take it off him'
an icer is something that ices or chills

explanation.surface: A pilot needs pressurised air from the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts run AIR, FORCE, OFF, ICER, with 'from' giving OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior military pilot or commander is literally someone who flies high.

clue.text: Turn gas up in the way needed to make Italian food

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

indicators.note: turn shows that the word gas is turned round to face the other way

explanation.surface: Turn up the gas on the stove to cook pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' (helped by 'up' in a down clue) reverses GAS to SAG, which goes 'in' LANE.
explanation.definitionFit: This layered pasta dish baked with sauce comes from Italy.

clue.text: Resign oneself to what players do in Happy Families

definitions.meaning: to quit a job, asking for the employment papers handed back on leaving

definitions.text: what players do in Happy Families
definitions.meaning: in this card game players request particular cards from each other

explanation.walkthrough: Happy Families is a traditional British children's card game in which players collect sets by requesting cards from others; 'cards' in Britain were also the documents an employee collected on leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitting employment was once done by requesting your insurance papers back, and requesting cards is the move in that game.

clue.text: What those with cash flow problems fly if they can raise the wind

definitions.text: What those with cash flow problems fly if they can raise the wind

parts.words: What those with cash flow problems fly if they can raise the wind
parts.note: to raise the wind is old slang for getting money, and flying one of these was raising cash on a worthless bill

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a toy flown on a breezy day, but 'raise the wind' means raise money, and 'fly a kite' is slang for passing a dud cheque or accommodation bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper toys on strings are flown in wind; in finance the same word names a dubious bill used to raise money.

clue.text: Take in Japanese game to an African state

parts.note: to take in someone is to con or deceive them
go is the Japanese board game of black and white stones

explanation.surface: Someone takes a Japanese board game to Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republic of the Congo is a country in central Africa, as is its larger neighbour.

clue.text: Pine which has not been cut?

definitions.meaning: to pine is to yearn or ache for something
hair or grass that has not been trimmed stays lengthy

explanation.definitionFit: Yearning is a verb sense of the word, and uncut things are of great length.

clue.text: Crushed lemon as a starter

indicators.note: crushing breaks something up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Squeezed lemon served as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of this fruit is a classic first course at a meal.

clue.text: Ancient city for a favourite Egyptian god

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: An old city chosen as a favourite by an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock-cut Nabataean city in Jordan dates from antiquity.

clue.text: Make believe in the possibility of preventative treatment?

definitions.meaning: to act as if something is so
to tend or look after someone before the illness comes

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word into PRE (before) and TEND (care for), which is what preventative treatment would be.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning is make-believe, and caring for a patient in advance is tending beforehand.

clue.text: Shake claret to a point where it becomes a thick syrup

indicators.note: shaking a bottle of wine jumbles its contents, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Wine shaken until it thickens into syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shake' rearranges CLARET plus E (a compass point) into the syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden syrup and black molasses are both kinds of this thick sugary liquid.

clue.text: You must have one if you want to "organise" instead of going home

definitions.text: You must have one if you want to "organise"
definitions.meaning: to play the organ (organ-ise) you need a stop pulled out
to stay out late rather than return home

explanation.walkthrough: 'Organise' is read as 'play the organ': an organ only sounds when a stop is drawn out.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ needs a drawn stop to sound, and staying out late is the phrasal verb's sense.

clue.text: Don't lie, but ignore the date

definitions.meaning: be upright rather than lying down
to fail to turn up for a romantic meeting

explanation.definitionFit: Being upright and jilting someone by not showing up are both senses of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: A stinging order

parts.note: a prickly plant that also names a Scottish order of chivalry

explanation.walkthrough: The Most Ancient and Most Noble Order of the Thistle is Scotland's highest order of knighthood; the plant pricks rather than stings, but 'stinging order' sounds like a sharp command.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly emblem of Scotland gives its name to the Scottish order of knighthood.

clue.text: What to do if you don't like the radio when driving on main roads

definitions.text: What to do if you don't like the radio
definitions.meaning: to switch a set off
to leave the highway for a side road

explanation.definitionFit: Switching a set off and leaving a highway are both senses of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: What the marksman did to pass with a first class mark

parts.note: to pass something is to OK it
A1 means first class, written with the letter I for the figure
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter passes the test with top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first class) is entered as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooter lines up the sights on a target before firing.

clue.text: Revise offer before it entails a penalty

indicators.note: to revise is to alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Changing a bid before it brings a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revise' signals the anagram; 'before' simply places it ahead of IT, and 'entails' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lost as a fine or punishment is this.

clue.text: Self-starters for a car

definitions.meaning: the prefix meaning self begins words like autobiography
short for automobile

explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-starters' looks like a car's ignition, but it is the Greek prefix for self that starts words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek combining form for self opens many words, and it is also a short word for motor car.

clue.text: Sort of key suitable for a child

definitions.meaning: a musical key with a flattened third, as opposed to major
in law, a person under the age of majority

explanation.definitionFit: Musical keys are major or this, and a person under age is legally one.

clue.text: In the middle of a safari?

definitions.text: In the middle of a safari?

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit in the centre of the words a safari

explanation.surface: A query about where you are when deep in the middle of an African safari.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S and I from the ends of SAFARI; the whole clue also describes being far away out on the plains.
explanation.definitionFit: On a trip deep in the African bush you are at a great distance from home.

clue.text: Free Security Council party

parts.note: the Security Council is a body of the UN, the United Nations
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Release from a Security Council celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or release a knot or clasp is to set it loose.

clue.text: Where boys learn only ten letters of the alphabet?

definitions.text: Where boys learn only ten letters of the alphabet?

parts.words: Where boys learn only ten letters of the alphabet?
parts.note: a boys' school whose name, split after its first letter and before its last, describes a run of ten letters of the alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English boys' public school near Windsor; its name splits as E TO N, which covers ten letters, E F G H I J K L M N.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous boarding school by the Thames is a place where boys are educated.

clue.text: THE very thing!

definitions.meaning: the word itself, which grammar classes as this part of speech
the genuine item, the real McCoy

explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians give 'the' this name, and 'the genuine article' means exactly what is wanted.

clue.text: It needs some tinkering by a roadman

definitions.text: It needs some tinkering by a roadman

parts.words: It needs some tinkering by a roadman
parts.note: a tinker mended holes in pots, and a road worker mends holes in the road surface

explanation.walkthrough: A tinker was a travelling mender of pots and pans; the road worker's version is filling a hole in the road, which shares the name of a pot with a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit in a road surface needs repair, and tinkers once fixed holes in cooking pots.

clue.text: Time Dan out for the muezzin

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: the page scan was misread: the setter's word is 'ran', taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: The prayer caller's time is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TIME and RAN; the muezzin calls Muslims to prayer from this mosque tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The slender tower of a mosque is where the caller to prayer stands.
